4. How the revised energy calculation works

I did not use the ideal half-second force ramp as a physical release law.

The proposed metering drive instead has introduced limits on:

Input torque and output torque.
Screw lead and gear ratio.
Rotating inertia.
Maximum displacement speed and acceleration.
Backlash per engagement.
Brake delay, braking torque and stop count.
Force observation errors and terminal force deadbands.

The current axial metering construction uses a 2 mm lead screw, 200:1 gearing, a 9.5 N·m output torque cap, 25 µm/s maximum displacement speed and a retained 4 kN path. The moving-force admission is lower, at 2 kN.

The observation loop uses measured force, measured displacement, time and progress history. It does not receive hidden contact stiffness or fault identity as decision inputs. An observed stall retains the load and requests a stocked drive exchange.

This addresses the problem that a slow or monotone force command can still excite a mode. It remains conditional on constructing and measuring the actual torque, inertia, friction, backlash and brake bounds.
